sections.heading: EPDM Roof Repair or a New EPDM Roof: Flat Roofing on Montclair Houses

runs.v: usually meet EPDM on a small roof: a porch roof, a modern kitchen addition, a dormer, or a garage behind the house, the low-slope architectural sections where EPDM is a popular choice. EPDM is commonly sold in 45-mil and 60-mil thicknesses, in rolls with widths ranging from 7.5 to 50 feet, so a new EPDM roof on a porch often goes on as one large sheet with minimal seams, and the seams that remain must be properly sealed with primer and seam tape to create watertight joints. EPDM roof repair makes sense while the membrane is still pliable and the leaks trace to one seam, puncture, or flashing; an aged EPDM membrane that has shrunk, cracked, or leaks at several seams usually calls for replacement, and a restoration coating can extend a sound but weathered membrane. EPDM needs minimal upkeep, but routine inspections, debris cleaning, and a check after major storms help prevent major issues and extend its lifespan. Newark Quality Roofing gives Montclair customers comprehensive solutions for flat roofing, from EPDM repairs to full roof replacements, with quality workmanship and careful attention to the flashing where the flat section meets the house wall and the shingles above, because installation quality is critical to longevity and a properly installed membrane is waterproofing that gives long lasting protection.

sections.heading: EPDM Rubber Roofing Installation Methods: Fully Adhered, Mechanically Fastened, Ballasted

runs.v: hold an EPDM roofing membrane in place. A fully adhered membrane is glued to the insulation or deck with bonding adhesives, the usual choice on houses; a mechanically fastened membrane is secured with metal fasteners and plates at the laps; and a loose laid, ballasted membrane is held down by stone or pavers on a commercial building or business rooftop whose structure can carry the weight. Whatever the assembly, the seams, the flashing, and the deck preparation decide long term performance, which is why installers matter as much as materials.

sections.heading: Downsides of EPDM Roofing Systems vs. TPO and Modified Bitumen

c.v: The downsides of EPDM rubber roofing

runs.v: are its seams, its puncture sensitivity, and its looks: standard black EPDM absorbs more solar heat than white reflective options, so it offers less energy efficiency than white TPO unless you choose reflective white EPDM, which helps reduce indoor cooling loads, or a reflective coating, and it is not attractive where a porch roof is visible from upstairs windows. In its favor, EPDM is highly resistant to UV exposure, ozone, and temperature fluctuations, handles thermal shock well, resists wind damage and harsh weather when properly installed, and performs well in the Northeast's extreme weather, with a proven track record from decades of use on flat and low slope roofs. It is often cited for low environmental impact, with low embodied energy and recyclable membranes, and it usually costs less than modified bitumen. TPO relies on heat-welded seams and modified bitumen adds a thicker, multi-ply surface for foot traffic, and the roofing industry uses EPDM roofing systems and both rivals on low slope roofs across residential and commercial properties.

faqs.q: How long does an EPDM rubber roof last on a Montclair flat or low-slope section?

runs.v: EPDM rubber roofing lasts 15 to 25 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart. The most common failures after 15 or more years are seam separation and flashing aging rather than membrane-field failure, so reseaming and resealing the failed detail can extend service life.

faqs.q: Can an aging EPDM roof in Montclair be repaired instead of replaced?

runs.v: Yes, when the damage stays localized and the rubber field stays sound, through reseaming and adhered rubber patches. Replacement follows when the membrane reaches its 15-to-25-year service life or seam and flashing failures spread across the roof.

faqs.q: Why does my Montclair EPDM roof keep leaking at the same seam?

runs.v: Seam separation is the most common EPDM failure, where the adhesive bonding two sheets breaks down before the rubber does, per HomeGuide membrane-repair guidance. Standing water compromises seams over time, and ponding held more than 48 hours counts as a defect, so the repair reseams the lap and corrects the drainage.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof on a Montclair storefront or multi-unit building require a permit?

runs.v: On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, while work on a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. Confirm with the Montclair construction office before work; N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires full removal when the membrane is water-soaked or already has two or more layers.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof in a Montclair historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: It can, mainly for work that changes a roof's appearance; in-kind repair is the simpler path. Confirm with the Montclair construction office before work, since properties in a historic district can need extra review; per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.

Final cost depends on roof size, slope, membrane thickness, and access.

faqs.q: Are rubber roof and EPDM the same?

runs.v: Usually, yes. EPDM is the synthetic rubber most people mean by a rubber roof, though TPO and PVC single-ply membranes are sometimes loosely called rubber too.

Roofing supply distributors and some home-improvement stores sell EPDM rolls, adhesives, and seam tape, but most manufacturer system warranties require installation by trained roofing contractors. Newark Quality Roofing installs and repairs EPDM as a roofing contractor.
